title: MEDI2004 W7 · Rational Drug Design
subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
content: How medicines are found — the shift from stumbling onto them to engineering them against a known target. Why it matters: single well-aimed molecules rewrote whole diseases. Penicillin's β-lactam ring is a reactive 'warhead' that irreversibly acylates the bacterial transpeptidase (penicillin-binding protein); because it mimics the D-Ala–D-Ala end of the cell-wall peptide the enzyme grabs it, then the strained ring jams the enzyme shut. Penicillin is selectively toxic because humans have no cell wall and no transpeptidase. In HIV, tipranavir is a protease inhibitor (blocks viral polyprotein cleavage so virions cannot mature) and maraviroc is an entry inhibitor (a CCR5 co-receptor antagonist) — hitting different points of the life-cycle. Discovery types: empirical/phenotypic (screen for an effect without knowing the target), rational/target-based (design against a defined target), and hybrid. The rational pipeline runs target hypothesis → hit → lead → lead optimisation → candidate → IND → clinical trials. Economics: each approved drug costs billions and ~10–15 years, with heavy attrition — only about 1 in 100 discovery projects reaches the market.

questions.question: Rational (target-based) drug design begins with knowledge of the drug's:
questions.explanation: Rational design starts from a defined molecular target and engineers a molecule to fit it, rather than screening blindly.

questions.question: Penicillin kills bacteria by attacking a structure that human cells do not have, the:
questions.explanation: Penicillin blocks bacterial cell-wall synthesis; humans lack a cell wall, which is why the drug is selectively toxic.

questions.question: Bringing a single new drug to market typically costs on the order of:
questions.explanation: Developing one approved drug costs billions of dollars, largely because so many candidates fail along the way.

questions.question: A protease inhibitor such as tipranavir treats HIV by blocking the virus from:
questions.explanation: HIV protease cleaves viral polyproteins into working parts; inhibiting it stops new virions from maturing.

questions.question: Empirical (phenotypic) drug discovery screens compounds for a useful effect without first knowing the:
questions.explanation: Empirical screening looks for a desired biological effect and identifies the target later, if at all.

questions.question: The reactive 'warhead' of penicillin that jams the bacterial enzyme is its:
questions.explanation: The strained four-membered β-lactam ring is highly reactive and covalently acylates the target enzyme, switching it off.

questions.question: Penicillin works because it structurally mimics the cell-wall building block:
questions.explanation: Penicillin mimics the terminal D-Ala–D-Ala of the peptidoglycan chain, so the transpeptidase binds it as if it were substrate.

questions.question: Selective toxicity means a drug harms the pathogen far more than the host by hitting a target that the host:
questions.explanation: The ideal antimicrobial hits a target unique to the pathogen (like the bacterial cell wall), sparing the host that lacks it.

questions.question: Maraviroc blocks HIV at a different step from a protease inhibitor because it prevents the virus from:
questions.explanation: Maraviroc is an entry inhibitor that antagonises the CCR5 co-receptor, stopping the virus fusing with and entering the host cell.

questions.question: Combining a protease inhibitor with an entry inhibitor in HIV is powerful because the two drugs act on:
questions.explanation: Hitting several stages of the viral life-cycle at once makes escape by resistance far harder — the logic of combination antiretroviral therapy.

questions.question: In the rational design pipeline, the first active compound found against a target is called a:
questions.explanation: A 'hit' is an initial compound showing activity against the target; it is later refined into a lead and then a candidate.

questions.question: Turning a promising hit into a lead involves chemically improving its potency, selectivity and:
questions.explanation: Lead optimisation tunes potency, selectivity and pharmacokinetic (drug-like) properties to make a molecule suitable for development.

questions.question: A hybrid discovery approach is best described as combining empirical screening with:
questions.explanation: Hybrid discovery blends phenotypic screening with rational, target-based design to draw on the strengths of both.

questions.question: Before a candidate can be tested in humans, it must gain approval to begin clinical trials, marked by the:
questions.explanation: The Investigational New Drug (IND) step authorises first-in-human testing after preclinical work supports the candidate.

questions.question: Roughly how many of every 100 drug-discovery projects finally reach the market?
questions.explanation: Attrition is severe: only about 1 in 100 discovery projects survives the funnel all the way to an approved medicine.

questions.question: The typical time from starting discovery to an approved drug is closest to:
questions.explanation: Discovery through approval usually spans about 10–15 years, reflecting the many sequential stages and failures.

questions.question: Structure-based drug design uses the three-dimensional shape of the target to design a molecule that:
questions.explanation: Knowing the target's 3D structure lets chemists design a molecule that fits its binding site precisely — the essence of rational design.

questions.question: Penicillin's block of the bacterial transpeptidase is effectively permanent because the β-lactam ring forms a bond that is:
questions.explanation: The ring acylates the enzyme's active-site serine covalently, so the block is irreversible until new enzyme is made.

questions.question: Bacteria commonly resist penicillin by producing β-lactamase, an enzyme that:
questions.explanation: β-lactamase hydrolyses the β-lactam ring before it can act, destroying the drug — a key mechanism of resistance driving side-chain redesign.

questions.question: A major advantage of rational over purely empirical discovery is that, from the start, it offers a clear:
questions.explanation: Knowing the target gives a defined mechanism that chemists can rationally optimise, unlike blind screening — though success is still not guaranteed.

questions.question: Because roughly 99 of 100 projects fail, the price of each marketed drug must effectively cover the cost of:
questions.explanation: The revenue from the one success has to pay for the 99 that failed, a central reason new medicines are so expensive.

questions.question: Targeting the CCR5 co-receptor rather than a viral enzyme means maraviroc acts on a molecule belonging to the:
questions.explanation: CCR5 is a human co-receptor the virus exploits; blocking this host protein prevents entry, a strategy distinct from hitting viral enzymes.

questions.question: Placing the stages in order, a molecule proceeds from hit to lead to:
questions.explanation: After a hit is optimised into a lead, the best lead becomes the development candidate that moves toward the IND and clinical trials.

questions.question: Designing an antiviral is often harder than an antibacterial because viruses replicate using the host's own:
questions.explanation: Viruses hijack host machinery, so there are fewer uniquely viral targets, making selective toxicity harder to achieve than with bacteria.

questions.question: Knowing a target enzyme's active-site shape most directly helps a chemist design a molecule with high:
questions.explanation: A 3D structure lets designers craft a molecule complementary to the binding site, maximising affinity and selectivity.

questions.question: The plague and HIV examples are used to show that a single new drug can change a disease's:
questions.explanation: Each case shows a drug turning a lethal disease into a treatable one — shifting the whole treatment paradigm, the payoff that justifies the cost.

questions.question: Re-engineering the penicillin side chain to defeat resistant bacteria is an early real example of:
questions.explanation: Changing one substituent to resist β-lactamase or broaden spectrum is deliberate structural modification — rational design applied to an existing scaffold.
